rich_summary: Kumbhakarna marches out of Lanka to face Rama’s monkey army and wades into battle with terrifying strength. The monkeys swarm him with trees, stones, and claws, but he laughs off the assault and even devours some of them. Sugriva attacks but is seized until Lakshmana intervenes, striking Kumbhakarna with powerful arrows. In a dramatic exchange, Lakshmana cuts off the giant’s arms, which miraculously multiply, forcing an even greater display of skill. Finally Lakshmana uses a Brahma weapon to slay the monstrous warrior, causing the Rakshasa troops to panic. Other Rakshasas, including Vajravega and Promathin, attempt retaliation but are killed by Hanuman and Nala. The section ends with Ravana, enraged by these losses, sending his formidable son Indrajit to challenge Lakshmana to a decisive duel.

highlight_spans.why: Transition into the episode where Kumbhakarna leaves the city and the confrontation with the monkey army begins.
The gruesome moment where Kumbhakarna laughs at the attackers and devours monkeys, emphasizing his terrifying nature.
Lakshmana’s decisive intervention—his arrow pierces Kumbhakarna and forces the release of Sugriva.
The supernatural moment when Kumbhakarna’s severed arms multiply, escalating the battle’s mythic scale.
Lakshmana destroys Kumbhakarna with the Brahma weapon, a pivotal victory that turns the momentum of the battle.
Ravana orders Indrajit to avenge the fallen generals, setting up the next major duel in the war.

top_scenes.scene_text: Gigantic Kumbhakarna stands amid the battlefield laughing as monkey warriors attack him with trees and stones while he devours them.
Lakshmana fires a golden-winged arrow that pierces straight through Kumbhakarna’s massive chest as Sugriva falls free from the giant’s grasp.
The monstrous Kumbhakarna grows enormous with many arms and heads before Lakshmana’s blazing Brahma weapon strikes him down like a thunderbolt-felled tree.
